subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — FinServe TCO discussion
messages:

Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — FinServe TCO discussion

Hi Aisha (and team),

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the open discussion. Quick recap of what we heard and the recommended next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of pain points and goals
- Cost pressure: Current LLM spend for the pilot is running ~10M tokens/month and is expected to grow 3–4x with expanded user traffic. Procurement’s stated target is to keep run-rate under ~$15k/mo for the first phase.
- Latency/UX: 95th percentile latency target of <300ms for chat flows (important for external customers).
- Quality: Need to preserve model quality for customer-facing generative responses (no aggressive response truncation).
- Ops: Desire to avoid building an inference stack in-house; want predictable billing and guardrails.

Redwood TCO levers we discussed (high level)
- Token economics: For the models we reviewed, hosted rate is roughly $0.0008 / 1k tokens for the generative model variant we suggested. With your 10M tokens/mo baseline, that’s ~ $8k/mo raw. However, without reuse/batching overheads, effective costs could be 30–50% higher depending on prompt size and repetition.
- Batching & continuous batching: Grouping simultaneous short requests can reduce per-token overhead and improve GPU throughput — estimated 10–25% savings in compute cost for chat-style traffic.
- KV/prefix caching: For high prompt reuse (shared system prompts, repeated few-shot examples), prefix caching can reduce generation tokens by 20–50% depending on reuse patterns.
- Quantization & model variants: Running a quantized model (8-bit) or a smaller variant for lower-criticality routes can reduce inference cost ~30–60% while preserving acceptable quality for many tasks.
- Dedicated capacity: If you reserve dedicated GPU pools, unit cost drops and latency tightens; break-even often happens once sustained monthly token volume is >30–40M tokens on heavy gen workloads.

Initial TCO takeaway (back-of-envelope)
- Baseline (hosted, no caching): ~$8k/mo (token charges) + infra/overhead = ~ $10–12k/mo
- With moderate caching + batching and mixed model variants: potential to get to ~$6–8k/mo for the same effective user experience.
- With dedicated/reserved capacity at scale (30M+ tokens/mo): possible to push to <$5k/mo equivalent depending on commit.

Next steps
1) I attached a TCO workbook (FinServe_TCO.xlsx) with a simple model you can tweak (traffic, prompt length, reuse). Please populate your expected monthly active users and average prompt/response lengths.
2) Marissa (cc’d) — our solutions engineer — will run a quick sensitivity analysis and propose a pilot configuration (batching policy + caching rules + model variant).
3) Aisha/Procurement: if you can confirm the $15k/mo threshold or provide the procurement cadence, we’ll prepare an initial pricing proposal + draft MA. I’m attaching a sample pricing PDF and our standard MA template for reference.
4) Proposed follow-up: 30-minute call next week to review the populated TCO and agree on pilot KPIs. Please share 2–3 windows that work.

If I missed anything or you want a different framing in the workbook, let me know — happy to iterate.

Thanks — Ben

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications: 
- Procurement confirms the target run-rate of ~$15k/mo for phase 1; if we can show clear cost reductions during pilot we have flexibility for expansion.
- Can you include a per-1k-token and per-request (avg prompt+response) line item in the workbook? Procurement wants to compare Redwood unit economics to our current vendor.
- We’d be interested in a 4-week pilot (non-prod) to validate end-to-end numbers — Marissa, can your team support a pilot that scopes batching and prefix caching with telemetry?

I’ve looped in procurement (procurement@finserve.com) to handle the MA/redline review once we have the pricing.

Two times that work for a follow-up next week: Tue 4/27 10:00–10:30am PT or Wed 4/28 2:00–2:30pm PT.

Best,
Aisha
